title: Log lifecycle tiering and schema evolution guidelines
body:
Purpose and scope:
This doc captures operational guidance for the full lifecycle of Redwood audit logs: from hot ingestion through indexing and tiered storage to long-term cold retention and eventual deletion. It focuses on practical rules for tiering, schema evolution (v2+), automated backfills, and known failure modes in the indexing/export pipelines (SIEM, warehousing). The goal is to consolidate engineering and security requirements so ops, SRE, and compliance teams have a single reference for retention decisions and remediation steps.

Key terms (quick):
- Hot store: low-latency indexed store used for immediate search/alerts (OpenSearch cluster).
- Warm store: compressed, queryable indices (fewer replicas, slower nodes).
- Cold/Archive: object store (S3) with lifecycle rules (Glacier/Archive) for compliance retention windows.
- Evidence bundle: tamper-evident copy of logs for legal hold with signed hashes and KMS-wrapped keys.
- Schema version: audit_log_v1, audit_log_v2, etc. Each version must be backward-compatible or have explicit migration plan.

Retention policy summary (compliance-driven):
- 90 days: hot search in OpenSearch (full index, instant queries).
- 1 year: warm indices in OpenSearch (replicas reduced, ILM rollover to warm).
- 7 years: cold archive in S3 (encrypted), accessible via controlled rehydration procedures for legal/eDiscovery.
- Legal hold: suspend deletion and create evidence bundle; retain checksum provenance.
Notes: retention durations are policy-driven; above are defaults for most customers but tenant-level overrides may exist.

Indexing strategy and ILM (OpenSearch/Elasticsearch):
- Use daily indices with rollover when index size > 50GB or age > 1d for high-volume tenants, otherwise use 7d windows.
- ILM phases: hot -> warm -> cold -> delete. Configure separate policies per tenant group (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
- Mapping: use explicit mappings for known fields (timestamp, tenant_id, user_id_hash, event_type, resource, action, outcome, request_id, rbac_version). Avoid dynamic mapping for top-level fields to prevent mapping explosion.
- Aliases: maintain read/write alias (audit-logs-write) that points to current hot index; search alias per retention window for queries.
- Shard sizing: target shards ~30–50GB post-compression. Use shard allocation awareness across AZs.

Schema evolution (v2 guidance):
- Version field: every log must include "schema_version" (e.g., "audit_log_v2").
- Additive changes only by default: new optional fields OK. Removal or renaming requires a migration window and backfill plan.
- Compatibility matrix: maintain a matrix in Confluence mapping which consumers (SIEM exports, internal alerting, data warehouse transforms) can read which versions.
- Transform functions: implement canonicalizers in the pipeline that can upgrade older messages to latest shape before indexing/exports. Canonicalizers are small, idempotent mapping steps in the ingestion stream.
- Example: v1 had "user_id" (plaintext). v2 has "user_id_hash" and a "pii_redaction" enum. The transformer must compute user_id_hash for v1 entries and set pii_redaction accordingly.

Ingestion pipeline (high-level):
- Sources -> Fluentd/Vector -> Kafka (topic: audit-raw) -> Stream processors (Flink/Spark Streaming) apply transforms -> audit-enriched topic -> Indexer (bulk writes to OpenSearch) AND archive-writer (S3 parquet).
- S3 archive is the canonical durable copy and source of truth for backfills and evidence bundles. Keep raw and enriched copies for 30 days to allow reprocessing.

Backfill and reindex patterns:
- Use S3 as the canonical input for backfills. Backfill pipeline (Airflow DAG): read parquet partitions, apply canonicalizer, write to temporary index, atomically swap alias.
- For schema changes that require reindex: run a staged backfill in a lower-cost cluster (reindex cluster), validate counts and diffs, then cut alias to new indices.
- Idempotency: all backfill jobs must be idempotent. Use deterministic document IDs (sha256(tenant + request_id + event_timestamp)) to avoid duplicates.

Failure modes and runbook (common):
1) Indexer bulk write failures (429/timeout)
   - Symptom: high bulk request rejections, growing lag in Kafka consumer lag, slow downstream alerts.
   - Immediate action: throttle the indexer (reduce batch size), add backpressure on consumer, switch to emergency warm nodes if available.
   - Long-term: increase index write capacity or reduce indexing QPS via sampling.

2) Schema mismatch causing mapping exceptions
   - Symptom: bulk writes failing with mapping errors referencing unexpected field type changes.
   - Immediate action: pause writes to affected index alias, create a new temporary index with relaxed mapping (use runtime fields or text) and resume writes to alias pointing to temp index. Notify owners.
   - Follow-up: run backfill/canonicalizer to normalize data types and reindex into correct mapping.

3) Kafka topic retention misconfigured -> data loss
   - Symptom: consumer seeks beyond earliest offset when attempting backfill; expected partitions missing old messages.
   - Immediate action: check S3 archives for canonical data; reconstruct topic using archived parquet for reprocessing.
   - Preventive: monitor head/tail offsets and set alerts when retention < 2x expected backfill window.

4) SIEM export failed batch or malformed payloads
   - Symptom: SIEM vendor rejects API with 4xx/5xx or partial acceptance.
   - Immediate action: pause export DAG, inspect error payloads, run sanitizer over archive for the period and retry with smaller batches.
   - Permanent fix: tighten schema validation before export and add contract tests (end-to-end) in CI.

Evidence bundles and legal hold
- When legal hold is requested: snapshot S3 partitions for requested time range into an evidence-bucket with immutable object lock enabled and versioning. Generate SHA256 manifest and sign manifest with KMS key. Store manifest pointer in audit metadata and notify Legal + Compliance.
- Do not delete or transition objects under an active evidence lock. Update deletion pipeline to check legal_hold index before any TTL action.

PII & redaction rules
- Redact at ingestion when possible. Fields flagged as PII must be replaced with one-way hash (salted tenant-specific) and set pii_redaction status. Raw plaintext containing PII must not remain in hot indices beyond 7 days unless explicitly required for an investigation with approved justification.
- Keys for hashing must be rotated per policy. Maintain rotation metadata so re-hashable material can be reprocessed only when permitted.

Monitoring and alerts
- SLOs: consumer lag < 15m for high-priority tenants, indexing error rate < 0.1%, archive write success 100% for each daily partition.
- Alerts: ILM phase failures, index growth anomaly, S3 lifecycle errors, rehydration job failures. Use runbook links in alert messages.

Operational playbook snippets (copy-paste safe):
- Delete-safe check before index delete:
  1) query legal_hold index for tenant/date range
  2) check evidence snapshot existence in evidence-bucket
  3) if any positive, abort deletion and escalate
- Rehydrate and search archived partition:
  1) kick off rehydrate job (S3 -> warm Parquet) via Airflow; attach canonicalizer
  2) write to temp index with alias audit-restore-<ticketid>
  3) notify requestor with temp query endpoint and TTL (default 72h)

Operational checklist before a major schema change: 
- Lock: small freeze on production schema writes (announce 48h)
- Create migration branch and canonicalizer code
- Run schema compatibility tests against last 90 days of archived data
- Schedule rolling backfill window (non-peak hours) and canary subset (1% tenants)
- Run integrity audits (counts, checksum diffs) and runbook signoff from Compliance

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide final retention window for dedicated customers with contractual overrides (legal needs a per-customer override flag).
- Define exact rotation cadence for hashing salts and where rotation metadata is stored (wallet or KMS tags).
- Formalize SLA for evidence bundle creation (target: 48 hours after legal hold request).

Appendix: minimal audit log example (recommended canonical shape v2)
- timestamp: 2025-01-01T12:34:56Z
- tenant_id: t-abc123
- schema_version: audit_log_v2
- event_type: permission.update
- resource: repos/my-model/config
- action: update
- actor_id_hash: sha256:xxxxx
- request_id: r-20250101-abcdef
- outcome: success
- rbac_version: v2
- pii_redaction: hashed
- meta: {"client_ip_truncated": "10.0.0.x"}  <-- note: meta must be small and typed

Contact and ownership:
- Primary: Aisha Patel (security infra)
- Backup: Marco Rivera (SRE)
- Compliance review owner: Evelyn Zhang

Note: this doc is intentionally pragmatic and ops-oriented — keep it close to the runbooks and link to the formal retention policy in Confluence for legal authority.
